tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: What a delivery costs, which packs exist, and the exact x402 payment requirements for each. Balance is counted in DELIVERIES, not money, and packs never expire. Call this before buying.

tools.name: get_docs
tools.description: One section of the machine documentation: quickstart, headers, signature, notice, errors, billing or limits. Omit `section` to get the whole document.

tools.name: get_service_status
tools.description: Whether the service is currently selling, on which network, and if not — why not. This is configuration, not liveness: the full health endpoint is at /health.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: Your tasks and their state. Needs your management token as an Authorization header on this connection.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description: A single task: schedule, destination, state, next run, and how many failures in a row it carries.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Register a schedule against a destination you have already verified. Idempotent on "name": the same name updates the existing task instead of creating a second one. Creating costs nothing; each delivery ATTEMPT costs one credit.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Change the schedule, destination, method, timeout, headers or body of an existing task. Omit a field to leave it unchanged — sending null is refused, because "unchanged" and "cleared" must not look the same. State is NOT editable here: use pause_task and resume_task.

tools.name: pause_task
tools.description: Stop firing until you resume. Nothing is charged while a task is paused.

tools.name: resume_task
tools.description: Start firing again on the schedule. Refused if your balance is empty — buy deliveries first.

tools.name: run_task_now
tools.description: Deliver immediately, outside the schedule. THIS COSTS ONE CREDIT per attempt, exactly like a scheduled firing, and a timeout or unreachable host is retried up to three times — so one call can cost up to three credits. Use it to test a destination.

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Move the task to the recycle bin. It stops firing immediately and can be restored for 30 days with restore_task; after that it is unrecoverable. Credits already spent are not refunded.

tools.name: restore_task
tools.description: Bring a task back from the recycle bin within 30 days. It comes back PAUSED — resume it explicitly.

tools.name: register_destination
tools.description: Claim an https:// URL you control. We answer with a challenge and a SIGNING SECRET that is shown ONCE and never again — store it before you do anything else; it is what lets you verify that a delivery really came from us. The permission covers that path and everything beneath it, nothing above. Veri

tools.name: verify_destination
tools.description: Verification is one request from us to the exact URL you registered: POST, headers X-402cron-Challenge: <value> and X-402cron-Event: verify, JSON body {"challenge":"<value>"}. Reply within 5 seconds, without a redirect, with a body that is the bare value or {"challenge":"<value>"}; we read the first

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.description: The URLs you have claimed and whether each is verified. The signing secrets are never shown again.

tools.name: delete_destination
tools.description: Remove a claimed URL. Refused while a task still points at it — delete the task first.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: register_destination, verify_destination, list_destinations · Private data: get_docs, list_tasks, register_destination, verify_destination, list_destinations · Public sink: register_destination, verify_destination · Destructive: get_task, run_task_now, delete_task, register_destination, verify_destination, delete_destination.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: register_destination, verify_destination, list_destinations · Private data: get_docs, list_tasks, register_destination, verify_destination, list_destinations · Public sink: register_destination, verify_destination · Destructive: get_task, run_task_now, delete_task, register_destination, verify_destination, delete_destination

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "register_destination" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
